'''Rudolph C. Hwa''' (born November 1, 1931) is an American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and ''[[Emeritus|Professor emeritus]]'' at the [[University of Oregon]]. His areas of interest include the [[strong interaction]], [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear dynamics]], [[Fluctuation theorem|fluctuations]], and [[quark–gluon plasma]]. He was elected an [[List of American Physical Society Fellows|American Physical Society Fellow]] in 1995.

== Early life and education ==
Hwa Chia-chao was born in [[Shanghai]], [[China]], in 1931.<ref>{{Cite web|date=October 1, 1962|title=Index to Naturalization Petitions, 1906-1991|url=https://www.ancestry.com/imageviewer/collections/2897/images/40797_292447-01397?usePUB=true&_phsrc=ro8755522&_phstart=successSource&usePUBJs=true&pId=35214|url-access=subscription|access-date=2021-12-28|website=www.ancestry.com}}</ref><ref name=":0"/> He arrived in the United States in 1949, and became a naturalized citizen in [[San Francisco]] in 1962.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Hwa|first=Rudolph C.|date=May 2020|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=https://casprofile.uoregon.edu/sites/casprofile2.uoregon.edu/files/cv/cv-820.pdf|access-date=December 27, 2021|website=University of Oregon}}</ref>

He completed three degrees in electrical engineering at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois Urbana]]: a B.S. in 1952, an M.S. in 1953, and a Ph.D. in 1957. Hwa earned his 1962 Ph.D. in physics at [[Brown University]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Hwa|first=Rudolph C.|date=May 2020|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=https://casprofile.uoregon.edu/sites/casprofile2.uoregon.edu/files/cv/cv-820.pdf|access-date=December 27, 2021|website=University of Oregon}}</ref> with a dissertation titled, ''Study of pion-hyperon resonances by dispersion relations in the unphysical sheet,'' advised by David Feldman.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Physics Tree - Rudolph C Hwa|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=752400|access-date=2021-12-27|website=academictree.org}}</ref>

== Career ==
Between 1962 and 1966, Hwa held research positions at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Radiation Laboratory]] and at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Princeton University|Princeton]]. His first faculty position was at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at [[Stony Brook University|State University of New York at Stony Brook]], and he joined the faculty of the University of Oregon in 1971.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rudolph Hwa {{!}} Department of Physics|url=https://physics.uoregon.edu/profile/hwa/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=physics.uoregon.edu}}</ref> He was named professor emeritus in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emeriti and Retired {{!}} Profile Categories {{!}} Department of Physics|url=https://physics.uoregon.edu/profiles/emeriti/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=physics.uoregon.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
